title: Adaptive Admin Step Executor / Runbook Taskifier
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an adaptive executor that converts legacy procedural runbooks into granular, idempotent tasks that can be scheduled, retried, and audited by the support tooling. The goal is to enable operators to run multi-step admin flows (maintenance, user remediation, capacity adjustments) as small, observable tasks with automatic dry-run, simulated validation, and safe rollbacks. This ticket covers the core executor, task schema, optimistic concurrency controls per-tenant, secret passthrough model, and a minimal UI surface for interactive replay and dry-run results. It should integrate with the existing task queue and audit log, support policy-driven timeouts/quotas, and emit structured telemetry for cost/latency analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Step definitions can be authored in YAML/JSON and translated to a normalized task graph
Executor supports dry-run mode that validates steps without executing side effects
Each step executes idempotently with output saved to the audit log and linkable to the original runbook
Per-tenant concurrency and rate limits enforced; default safe limits applied for new accounts
Secrets are handled via KMS-wrapped references and never appear in logs; integration test with KMS connector
Automatic rollback policy available and exercised by test harness for >=3-step flows
Telemetry emitted for step latency, success/failure reasons, and tokens consumed for any LLM-driven steps
tasks: Spike: canonical task schema and YAML -> task-graph compiler (owner: Lena)
Prototype executor that runs no-op steps for dry-run and logs simulated outputs
Integrate KMS secret reference resolution and validate onboarding flow
Add tenancy-aware concurrency limiter and per-tenant quota checks
Build audit log links and backfill adapter to existing observability pipeline
Create test harness with synthetic runbooks and rollback verification
Design a compact console surface for step replay + dry-run results (PM/Design sync)
Document developer API and migration notes for oncall teams
